title: R One-Liners from the Shell
text: rush brings R command line. Run R expression, wrangle CSV, query Parquet file SQL, draw plot right terminal — without opening R session writing script. R wonderful ecosystem working data, reaching usually means launching R, loading packages, reading files hand. rush collapses single command can pipe, redirect, drop shell pipeline — R becomes just another Unix tool, home next grep, awk, jq. hood, invocation assembles small, self-contained R script runs ir, R interpreter launcher r-lib. script declares package dependencies #| frontmatter, ir installs whatever needs fly. means rush stays lightweight, never manage library packages just run one-liner.

title: R One-Liners from the Shell
text: One-liners, scripts. Evaluate R expression straight shell. Pipeline-native. Reads standard input writes standard output, composes every command-line tool. Reads . CSV delimited text, Parquet, DuckDB databases — chosen automatically file extension. Query SQL. sql command runs DuckDB queries directly files, import step required. Plots terminal. plot command renders ggplot2 graphics ANSI/ASCII art, saves PNG, PDF, . Zero dependency management. Packages resolved demand ir.

title: R One-Liners from the Shell
text: CSV default. Use --delimiter (-d) separators ---header (-H) files without header row:
code: rush run 'df |> dplyr::filter(mpg > 22) |> dplyr::select(mpg, cyl, hp)' mtcars.csv #> mpg,cyl,hp #> 22.8,4,93 #> 24.4,4,62 #> 22.8,4,95

title: R One-Liners from the Shell
text: Files ending .parquet .pq read nanoparquet — flags needed. Point --output (-o) .parquet file write one, makes rush quick way convert formats:
code: # Convert CSV to Parquet... rush run --output mtcars.parquet 'df' mtcars.csv  # ...then read it straight back rush run 'head(df, 3)' mtcars.parquet #> mpg,cyl,disp,hp,drat,wt,qsec,vs,am,gear,carb #> 21,6,160,110,3.9,2.62,16.46,0,1,4,4 #> 21,6,160,110,3.9,2.875,17.02,0,1,4,4 #> 22.8,4,108,93,3.85,2.32,18.61,1,1,4,1

title: R One-Liners from the Shell
text: Point rush DuckDB database (.duckdb .ddb) every table read dfs list, keyed table name: database holds single table, also bound df convenience, one-table database behaves just like single input.

title: R One-Liners from the Shell
text: Sometimes SQL simply clearest way express want — especially joins aggregations. sql command runs DuckDB query directly files, import step. file becomes relation named file, can reference right query: DuckDB reads file , works datasets far larger memory — filtering aggregation happen inside DuckDB, result comes back R. CSV files read read_csv_auto, Parquet read_parquet, .duckdb database attached tables addressed name.table. makes joins across whole database natural: result query ordinary data frame, everything else composes usual — pipe onward, save --output, including back Parquet:
code: rush sql "SELECT cyl, ROUND(AVG(mpg), 1) AS avg_mpg, COUNT(*) AS n           FROM mtcars GROUP BY cyl ORDER BY cyl" mtcars.parquet #> cyl,avg_mpg,n #> 4,23.3,3 #> 6,20.1,5 #> 8,16.5,2 rush sql "SELECT c.name, SUM(o.amount) AS total           FROM shop.customers c JOIN shop.orders o ON c.id = o.cust           GROUP BY c.name ORDER BY total DESC" shop.duckdb #> name,total #> Carol,65 #> Alice,55 #> Bob,10 rush run 'head(mtcars, 5)' | rush sql "SELECT cyl, mpg FROM stdin WHERE mpg > 21" - #> cyl,mpg #> 4,22.8 #> 6,21.4

title: R One-Liners from the Shell
text: plot command builds ggplot2 graphic data. Choose columns --x, --y, --color, friends, sensible geom guessed (override --geom). Show generated script --dry-run see exactly run: Run terminal plot drawn right ANSI/ASCII art. Redirect output file instead rush writes image, picking device extension:  Terminal plotting relies three packages CRAN — devout, miniansi, devoutansi — need install . rush declares generated script’s frontmatter, ir fetches GitHub first time needed.
code: rush plot --dry-run --x mpg --geom density --fill 'factor(cyl)' mtcars.csv #> #!/usr/bin/env -S ir run #> #| packages: #> #|   - rlang #> #|   - cli #> #|   - tibble #> #|   - readr #> #|   - ggplot2 #> #|   - fs #> #|   - github::coolbutuseless/devout #> #|   - github::jeroenjanssens/miniansi #> #|   - github::coolbutuseless/devoutansi #> #|   - janitor #>  #> .rush <- list( #>   output = NULL, #>   output_format = "delim", #>   width = NULL, #>   height = NULL, #>   units = "in", #>   dpi = 300, #>   delimiter = ",", #>   has_post = FALSE #> ) #>  #> library(ggplot2) #> df <- janitor::clean_names(readr::read_delim("mtcars.csv", delim = ",", col_names = TRUE)) #> result <- ggplot(df, aes(x = mpg, fill = factor(cyl))) + geom_density() #>  #> #~~~ Output dispatch (added by rush) ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ #> .has_tty <- isatty(stdout()) #> .stdout_binary <- function() { #>   if (.Platform$OS.type == "windows") file("stdout", "wb", raw = TRUE) #>   else file("/dev/stdout", "wb", raw = TRUE) #> } #>  #> out <- .rush$output #> w <- .rush$width #> h <- .rush$height #> if (is.null(out)) out <- if (.has_tty) "ansi" else "png" #>  #> if (out %in% c("ansi", "ascii")) { #>   if (is.null(w)) w <- cli::console_width() #>   devoutansi::ansi(width = w, height = h, plain_ascii = TRUE, char_lookup_table = 2) #>   if (!.rush$has_post) { #>     result <- result + #>       ggplot2::theme_minimal() + #>       ggplot2::theme(panel.grid = ggplot2::element_blank()) #>   } #>   print(result) #>   invisible(grDevices::dev.off()) #> } else { #>   if (fs::path_ext(out) == "") { #>     output_filename <- tempfile() #>     device <- out #>     cat_output <- TRUE #>   } else { #>     output_filename <- out #>     device <- NULL #>     cat_output <- FALSE #>   } #>   if (is.null(w)) w <- 6 #>   if (is.null(h)) h <- 4 #>   ggplot2::ggsave(output_filename, result, device = device, #>                   width = w, height = h, units = .rush$units, dpi = .rush$dpi) #>   if (cat_output) { #>     contents <- readBin(output_filename, raw(), n = 1e8) #>     writeBin(contents, .stdout_binary()) #>   } #> } rush plot --x mpg --geom density --fill 'factor(cyl)' mtcars.csv > ../man/figures/mtcars.png

text: script --dry-run prints throwaway — complete, self-contained ir script. Redirect file reproducible artifact can version, share, run later, long one-liner scrolled shell history: #!/usr/bin/env -S ir run shebang first line makes file directly executable. ir reads #| frontmatter, installs packages script declares, runs — saved script carries dependencies needs nothing ir target machine: also handy tweaking: dump rush one-liner file, edit generated R something rush express directly, run ir run analysis.R.
code: rush run --dry-run 'df |> dplyr::filter(mpg > 21)' mtcars.csv > analysis.R head -3 analysis.R #> #!/usr/bin/env -S ir run #> #| packages: #> #|   - rlang chmod +x analysis.R ./analysis.R 2>/dev/null #> mpg,cyl,disp,hp,drat,wt,qsec,vs,am,gear,carb #> 22.8,4,108,93,3.85,2.32,18.61,1,1,4,1 #> 21.4,6,258,110,3.08,3.215,19.44,1,0,3,1 #> 24.4,4,146.7,62,3.69,3.19,20,1,0,4,2 #> 22.8,4,140.8,95,3.92,3.15,22.9,1,0,4,2
